title: Tenant correlation IDs, adaptive sampling, and SLOs for analytics ingest & processing
creator: Ava Sato
description: Goal: Provide reliable tenant-level observability for the analytics ingest and processing pipeline while controlling telemetry cost. Deliverables: 1) stable tenant-correlation-id (tcid) propagation across frontend -> ingest -> processing -> storage, 2) an adaptive sampling scheme that preserves error traces and a small fraction of normal traces per tenant, 3) clear SLIs/SLOs and per-tenant dashboards for ingest latency and processing success rate, and 4) a rollout/runbook that minimizes production risk and telemetry spend.
acceptance_criteria: tcid is generated at edge (if absent) and included in HTTP headers, Kafka message headers, and tracing spans for 100% of events in canary cluster
adaptive sampler is deployed to OTEL collector with default policy: retain all error traces, at-least-0.1% baseline trace sampling per tenant, and dynamic bump to 5% for tenants with >0.5% error-rate
Grafana dashboard 'Ingest: Tenant SLOs' shows p50/p95 ingest latency and processing success rate by tenant; alerts trigger when slo breaches persist >5m
end-to-end test harness validates trace-linking using tcid for 95% of synthetic traces and includes cost delta estimates for storage/ingest
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Scoped work with product and DS. Decided tcid format: 128-bit hex (uuidv4-like) to avoid collisions and PII leakage.
2026-02-20: Prototype propagation implemented in ingress lambda and kafka-producer helper. Added header X-Redwood-TCID.
2026-02-28: OTEL collector sampling POC using tail-based and probabilistic hybrid sampler. Early metrics show 6x reduction in trace volume with current policy.
2026-03-05: Dashboard templates created in Grafana (panel ids: 8321, 8322). Working on tenant-filtering controls and RBAC for viewing high-cardinality metrics.
2026-03-10: Safety rollout plan approved by SRE. Dark launch for 2 weeks, then 10% traffic for 72h, monitor cost & SLOs, then gradual ramp to 100% if stable.
comments: PM (Liam O'Connor): Prioritize error-trace retention for high-value customers. Provide per-tenant cost estimate so SRE can budget.
Design (Maya Chen): Avoid exposing user-level IDs in spans. Use tenant hash and optional sample-key for linking UI requests to events.
SRE (Priya Nair): Concern about high-cardinality labels. Suggest truncating long attributes and using 'tenant_bucket' for routing dashboards to avoid 10k+ series explosion.
Eng review (Rafael Gomez): Recommend OpenTelemetry collector + sampling processor; avoid custom in-app samplers to keep behavior consistent across languages.
Security (Anita Rao): Confirmed tcid is non-PII and non-reversible; security review required for any change that adds request-level IDs to logs.
rollout_plan: Dark launch: enable tcid header and trace propagation in staging and a shadow ingest cluster for 14 days. Measure trace link rate, storage delta, and SLI stability. Canarize to 10% traffic for 72h; pause on any SLO regression > 2x baseline or cost spike > 40%. If stable, incremental ramp to 50% then 100% over 7 days. Post-rollout: keep adaptive sampling defaults for 30 days and re-evaluate thresholds.
tradeoffs_and_notes: Trade-offs: higher sampling retains signal but increases storage/cost. Tail-based sampling keeps error signal but requires additional buffering and compute in OTEL collector. We intentionally avoid adding user-level identifiers to traces/logs to reduce privacy risk and cardinality. Use of tenant_bucket reduces granularity for large customers but keeps dashboards performant.
